subject: general
question: Where are waste products stored within a plant cell?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vacuoles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vacuoles** are membrane-bound organelles present in plant cells.
 
• They play a crucial role in storing nutrients, waste products, and maintaining turgor pressure within the cell.
 
• The vacuole in a plant cell is large and centrally located, occupying a significant portion of the cell's volume.
 
• Besides waste storage, vacuoles also store essential compounds such as ions, sugars, and amino acids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria**

 
 
• They are known as the powerhouse of the cell because they generate most of the cell's supply of ATP, used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• Mitochondria are not involved in storing waste products.
 
 
 
• **Golgi Bodies**
 
 
• Also known as the Golgi apparatus, they are involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or for use within the cell.
 
• Golgi bodies do not play a role in storing waste products.
 
 
 
• **Lysosomes**
 
 
• They are membrane-bound organelles that contain enzymes to break down waste materials and cellular debris.
 
• While lysosomes do help in waste processing, they do not store waste products.
 
 

The correct answer is **Option 2**__.
